intro: Every group of people in the world has special days. They light lamps, dance in parades, cook favorite foods and remember loved ones. They also play games, sing songs and tell stories. These things make up a big part of a people's culture, or way of life.

In this unit you will visit Carnival in Brazil, Lunar New Year in China and Korea, Diwali in India and Día de los Muertos in Mexico. You will hear mariachi and flamenco, play chess and soccer, and meet Anansi and the Monkey King. You will also see festivals right here in Chicago.

By the end, you will be able to explain why people celebrate. You will compare two traditions from different places. You will also trace how music, games and stories travel and blend into something new.
bigQuestion: What can the ways people celebrate, play and tell stories teach us about what they care about?

timeline.t: Chaturanga, an early form of chess, is played in India
Journey to the West, the story of the Monkey King, is written in China
The Declaration of Independence is approved on July 4
Oktoberfest begins in Munich; Mexico's call for independence rings out
The Brothers Grimm publish their first book of fairy tales
The Football Association writes the modern rules of soccer in England
Horace Wilson teaches baseball in Japan
Tokyo gives cherry trees to Washington, D.C.
The first Bud Billiken Parade marches in Chicago
Chicago first dyes its river green for St. Patrick's Day
UNESCO lists mariachi as an important living tradition

words.d: the way of life of a group, including its food, music, games, stories and beliefs
a special time when a community celebrates together
a way of doing things passed down from older people to younger people
the traditions, language and history that a group passes down
the time when crops are gathered from the fields
a calendar that counts months by the moon
a home altar with photos, candles, flowers and food for loved ones who have died
something a group of people usually does, often for a long time
the pattern of strong and soft beats in music
a story told out loud and passed down over many years
a clever story character who wins by using wits instead of strength
to mix two or more things into something new

choices: A festival of parades, music and costumes before Lent
A day to remember the dead
test.why: Carnival is a huge festival of samba, costumes and parades held just before Lent.

test.q: Why does the date of Lunar New Year move each year?
choices: It follows a calendar based on the moon
It is picked by a contest
test.why: Lunar New Year follows a lunar calendar, which counts months by the moon.

test.q: What do Diwali lamps stand for?
test.why: The lights of Diwali stand for good winning over evil.

test.q: In the chapter story, why does Lucía decorate a sugar skull?
test.why: Lucía and her grandmother make the skull for Día de los Muertos to remember Grandpa Tomás.

test.q: Which festival began with a royal wedding in 1810?
test.why: Oktoberfest began in Munich with the wedding of Crown Prince Ludwig and Princess Therese.

choices: The Japanese custom of enjoying cherry blossoms
test.why: Hanami means flower viewing, the custom of gathering under cherry blossoms in spring.

test.q: Which of these is a festival mainly about history?
test.why: Mexican Independence Day remembers Miguel Hidalgo's call for freedom in 1810.

test.q: Which Chicago celebration began in 1929 in Bronzeville?
test.why: The Bud Billiken Parade began in 1929 and marches through Bronzeville.
Flamenco comes from Andalusia, with a large role played by the Roma people.

test.q: Which instrument is shaped like an hourglass and comes from West Africa?
test.why: The talking drum is hourglass-shaped, and squeezing its cords changes its pitch.

test.q: How are cricket and baseball alike?
choices: Both are played with the feet
One player throws, one bats and the batting team scores runs
test.why: Cricket and baseball are bat-and-ball cousins where the batting team scores runs.

test.q: The word checkmate comes from which language?
test.why: Checkmate comes from the Persian shah mat, meaning the king is helpless.

choices: A clever spider from Akan folktales
test.why: Anansi is a trickster spider from the folktales of the Akan people of Ghana.

test.q: What did the Brothers Grimm want to do with folktales?
choices: Preserve them so they would not be forgotten
test.why: The Grimms wrote the tales down so they would not be lost.

test.q: Which is the best example of cultures blending?
choices: A family eats only one kind of food
A game stays in one village
K-pop mixes Korean songs with American hip-hop
A story is never told again
test.why: Blending means mixing into something new, like K-pop mixing Korean and American music.

write.prompt: Choose two celebrations, games or stories from this unit. Do they show that people around the world care about some of the same things? Make a claim. Use two or three facts from the unit to support it, and explain how each fact supports your claim.
tips: Name each tradition and the place it comes from.
Use unit words like tradition, heritage, custom or blend.
Tell how the two are alike and how they are different.
Describe every culture with respect, the way its own people would.
End by telling what you learned about people from your two examples.
